blocking_conditions: B1 (F-DG7-996, Medium, mandatory, OPEN, owner delivery-orchestrator): 'node tools/gates/validate.mjs --stage DG7' reports 57 write-once errors. Files committed under docs/delivery/runs/DG7 were later deleted or modified: the runner's transient .pre-config.txt, .pre-snapshot.json, .post-snapshot.json and uncompressed transcript.jsonl, swept into history by concurrent commits. The commits are f6686f0d7 (REV-QA-R5), b4f501c3f (DO-J2), 3b72c507f (DO-E2, DO-J2), 8d0abc3f9 (QA-D), 12229e6b6 (AN-P7) and cabf14268 (QA-C). The final run records are intact, but rules.mjs checkReviewRounds forbids any deletion under runs/ in history. The release-auditor cannot waive this. Clearing it needs a decision by the orchestrator and the user, for example a clean re-gate on a new base (D-184/D-190/D-238) or a reviewed gate-rule change, and then a new audit.

B2 (F-DG7-997, Medium, mandatory, OPEN, owner delivery-orchestrator): stages.json DG7 review_rounds 7, 8 and 9 record frozen_at 2026-11-16T18:39:59Z, but the committed manifest 0d71d4456adaac94 and candidate.frozen_at record 2026-11-16T18:39:12Z. The validator reports 'frozen_at/source_commit differ from its committed manifest' for all three rounds. stages.json is meta-excluded, so a correction needs no re-freeze.

B3 (F-DG7-998, Medium, mandatory, OPEN, owner delivery-orchestrator): findings.json verification blocks of 19 CLOSED_VERIFIED findings carry qa-verifier's sidecar entry: F-DG7-913, 914, 953, 954, 955, 956, 915, 935, 960, 961, 962, 963, 920, 921, 940, 971, 923, 942 and 972. The validator selects code-security-reviewer's entry (domain-reviewer's for 971), giving 57 errors (role, invocation and evidence differ). Every sidecar in each deciding round is PASS by a non-owner, so the closures are substantively valid. findings.json is meta-excluded. A re-import with tools/gates/import-findings.mjs that matches the validator's selection is needed.

B4 (F-DG7-999, Medium, mandatory, OPEN, owner delivery-orchestrator): stages.json DG7 review round 5 lists records.qa-verifier = docs/delivery/reviews/DG7/round-5/qa-verifier.json, which the killed run f4c61bca never wrote (D-278). The validator reports the record and its verifications sidecar's record as not found (2 errors). It tolerates an interrupted run's sidecars only when the record is neither listed nor on disk (D-034). Also: F-DG7-971.reported_in names that missing file.

B5: consequently REQ-DLV-014's gate clause ('shown by validate.mjs --stage DG7 at the gate') and REQ-DLV-005's gate clause are not met. After B1-B4 are repaired and imported, a new release audit must re-run validate --stage DG7 with a gate record present. Every other condition checked in this audit holds: identity, provenance, verdicts, the substance of every finding, pre-freeze evidence, evidence honesty, the protocol-hit and K11 decisions, decisions and the product/engineering gate separation.
notes:
DG7 is an engineering delivery gate only. This record grants no real business, Finance or IT approval and implies nothing about product gates G1-G6. Product G6 never implies DG7. The demo data and approvals in the evidence are synthetic and labelled as such, #0078FF is a provisional brand token, and nothing claims official PMI status or certification.

Why BLOCKED: the assignment requires that every error 'validate --stage DG7' reports concern only this in-flight run. With a gate record present, the validator reports 119 other errors, from four record-integrity defects in delivery records (B1-B4). None changes the product or the candidate. The product, the three round-7 reviews and every prior finding's substance pass this audit. The earlier reviewers could not see these errors because 'validate --stage DG7' stops at 'gate DG7: file not found' when no gate record exists. The freeze-time check that D-277 introduced has the same limit. Recommendation for the gate rules' owner: run the record checks even when the gate record is absent, through the reviewed tools/gates change process.

F-DG7-973 (Low, not mandatory) stays accepted as an observation. It is accepted by the user's decision (progress.md, 2026-11-16), by its reporter qa-verifier (round 8) and by the release-auditor (round 8, confirmed here). The acceptance record's owner is delivery-orchestrator, and the follow-up, a dated ADR-0071 amendment, is owned by solution-architect.

Decisions carried to the next audit, unless something changes: the D-270 protocol hits (C2, C3, C5) and the A27 K11 partial do not on their own block DG7, and the D-274 Q19 extension is accepted.
